subject: Intermittent silent responses from hosted API — statuspage draft and customer alert
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-27T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: spikes of empty/partial responses observed in usw1 (initial detection)

Team,

We started seeing a small but consistent class of requests returning an empty body (HTTP 200 with zero tokens streamed) from the hosted inference cluster in us-west-1 starting ~09:04 PDT. Impact looks concentrated on the streaming endpoint for medium-length prompts (avg seq len ~1k). Quick notes: 

- Scope: ~2.6% of requests across customer buckets, concentrated on a handful of noisy prefixes that use prefetch/prefix-cache.
- Symptom: request accepted, connection held open ~100-300ms, then client receives no token chunks; logs show no generation frames emitted.
- Initial mitigation attempt: restarted prefetch workers for one pool; results inconclusive.

I've attached a short trace (prefetch-trace-20260827.txt) and a screenshot of the request queue snapshot. I'm putting this as P1 on the on-call channel and will join the bridge.

I suspect a race between our prefix cache invalidation routine and the streaming worker's readiness check; engineering investigating.

Irene

Subject: Re: intermittent failures — proposed customer-facing statuspage update (please review)

Amit / MindPath team,

Thanks for the flag — we're actively investigating an issue that can cause some requests to return no generated tokens from the hosted API in the us-west-1 region. We are preparing a statuspage notification now and wanted to share the draft and mitigation plan before publishing. Please let us know if you want additional wording or have specific customers we should call out.

Draft statuspage message (short):
"""
Incident: Intermittent empty responses from hosted inference (us-west-1).
We are investigating a condition causing a small percentage of streaming requests to return no generated tokens. Some customers may observe blank responses or apparent timeouts for affected prompts. Engineers have deployed mitigations and are monitoring.
"""

Planned mitigations:
- Route affected traffic to a fallback model variant without prefetch for the affected pools (immediate).
- Disable the prefix cache invalidation job for 1 hour while we validate a fix (if safe).
- Continue rolling a code patch to ensure readiness checks are gated on cache validity.

Marissa / Irene — can you publish to status.redwoodinference.com and include INF-4829? I propose we send this in ~10 minutes once we confirm the routing rule is in place.

Sean

Status summary posted:
- Incident ID: USW1-5821
- Impact: A small percentage of streaming requests in us-west-1 may return zero tokens or appear to stall.
- Current status: Investigating (engineering on-call reproducing; routing mitigation in progress).
- Mitigation: Traffic to affected pools is being routed to a fallback model variant without prefetch; this reduces the observed blank-response rate immediately.
- ETA for removal of fallback: TBD; we will update within 2–3 hours after validation.

Actions taken so far:
- Fallback routing applied to the noisy pools at 09:52 PDT.
- Prefix cache invalidation job disabled for 1 hour while investigating.
- INF-4829 created and assigned to engineering on-call.

We will update the incident page and loop back here as soon as we have confirmation the rate has returned to baseline.

Marissa

Subject: Post-incident summary: USW1 empty-response incident (root cause & next steps)

Amit / MindPath team —

Thanks for your patience while we investigated. Summary and follow-up from the engineering side: 

What happened (root cause):
- A race condition in the prefix cache invalidation code caused the streaming worker to believe a required prefetch had completed when, in a small subset of timing windows, the cache had been invalidated mid-read. This left the generation worker with no ready tokens to enqueue for streaming, resulting in an HTTP 200 with zero token frames for ~2–3% of requests on affected pools. Replication steps and traces are attached.

What we did to remediate: 
- Immediate: routed traffic to fallback model variants without prefetch for affected pools (reduced blank responses within ~10 minutes).
- Short-term fix: disabled the invalidation job and rolled a readiness-check patch that verifies cache presence before signaling worker readiness (deployed at 11:40 PDT).
- Verification: synthetic load tests and control-plane checks show the blank-response rate back to baseline by 13:10 PDT.

Customer impact: MindPath observed ~3% of live traffic showing failed predictions between 09:04–11:40 PDT. No data was corrupted or lost; some sessions fell back to cached predictions as Amit noted.

Next steps / commitments: 
- We will run an expanded regression test across prefix/prefetch variants and include a chaos test for cache invalidation by Sept 10.
- We will add a post-incident control-plane audit and share logs for the affected time range with your SREs.
- As a goodwill gesture, we will apply a 10% service credit for the usage during the incident window; Marissa will follow up with billing.
- We propose a 30-minute postmortem call with MindPath on Aug 31 at 10:00 PDT to walk the traces and mitigation details. Please confirm if that works.

If you want additional artifacts now, the drive folder is linked here: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-mindpath-incident-notes (contains traces, runbooks, and the INF-4829 owner log).

Irene Choi
Staff SWEng, Inference Platform
Redwood Inference
